This appears to be a CBP ruling on a medical gas "life support gas-line system" (likely a Amico or similar product). The components are packaged as a system and work together as a valve system, so classification is under heading 8481 (taps, cocks, valves). The composite machine / set rule would apply, with the principal function being regulating gas flow.

Within 8481, the options are:
- 8481.10: pressure-reducing valves
- 8481.20: valves for oleohydraulic or pneumatic transmissions
- 8481.30: check valves
- 8481.40: safety or relief valves
- 8481.80: other appliances
- 8481.80.90: other, including manually operated valves of iron or steel (8481.80.30) and others.

The system consists of regulators (pressure-reducing), shutoff valves, and check valves. The overall system is a valve system for regulating gas flow, with manually actuated shutoff valves and pressure regulators. I think CBP classified it under 8481.80.90 (other appliances), specifically 8481.80.9050 (other, other). Alternatively, 8481.10.0090 would apply if pressure-reducing was deemed the principal function. I will go with 8481.80.9050.

{"hts_code": "8481.80.9050", "reason": "The packaged gas manifold, zone valve box, and outlet function together as a valve system regulating gas flow, classified as other taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances of heading 8481 under GRI 1 and 3(b)."}
